NgraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale:
This bundle is the second small slice of the current-only CLI policy. It completes the review and selected-close consumers that the first slice (C-CURRENT-VALIDATION-BOUNDARY-1-D8D7DF85) explicitly left to dependent bundles, and it repairs two teaching rows that became false or misleading in light of the boundary. The normative source of truth is `spec.xml`; nothing here adds a requirement.
Two audit findings shape the selected-close design. First, the existing evaluator's `isAppliedArchiveBundle` early return means a missing or invalid spec, or a present non-applied status, never reaches validation; the validator must classify the selected directory phase before it reads parsed status. Second, the exported validators accept a legacy `<Criterion>` carrying an explicit `CloseEvidence`, more than one direct `CloseEvidence` block on one `AC-*`, and nested `CloseEvidence`: the command is then skipped or only the first block runs while the verdict still records `pass`. Validator reuse alone cannot close that gap, so a narrow selected-close evidence-consumption guard lives in the already-scoped `src/gates/ledger.ts` and its test file. The guard refuses explicit unconsumable evidence before evaluation and preserves ordinary `AC-*` criteria and meaningful legacy criteria that genuinely declare no evidence. Authority review also requires protected Git file type/executable mode and staged changes to be checked; the archive instrument skips the excluded own directory before traversal and refuses unsupported read types. These project-local Commands use the configured POSIX shell (here `/bin/zsh -lc`) and Bun, with no Windows-runner guarantee or CLI runner change.
The reviewed conceptual diagrams below are explanatory. They are not instructions to introduce new classes. Every binding behaviour is repeated in the spec's acceptance criteria.

Alternatives.Alternative: Keep the archived-plan review notices as informational (`review.historical-path-absent`) and make no review change. Rejected: under the current-only policy an unrelated archived plan is opaque history, and keeping it a current review input preserves a global content read of archives and a current output that depends on archived bytes. The counterweight is answered instead by active-plan refusal plus strict selected current-close validation.

Make the selected current-close validator use `validateNgraceProject` or enumerate archives so the selected record is checked through the whole-project surface. Rejected: `validateNgraceProject` walks active and archive directories and the archive branch is deliberately opaque; it would re-introduce archive discovery and validate unrelated bundles rather than only the selected record.

Add a new artifact-local selected-bundle validation wrapper in `src/artifact/grammar.ts`. Rejected as unnecessary for the schema/coverage half: the exported `validateChangeArtifact` and `validateSpecPlanCoverage` already provide artifact-local validation on parsed artifacts and add no global discovery. It is insufficient for the evidence-consumption half, which is implemented as the narrow guard in `src/gates/ledger.ts`, so grammar source and tests stay unforced.

Make every warning-severity issue refuse the selected close. Rejected: these advisory choices are deliberately non-refusing, and rejecting them is unrelated to preventing malformed or silently skipped selected evidence.

Add gate-verdict warning output so the selected validator can report advisory warnings. Rejected: it would require a new output contract and likely force `src/gates/command.ts` into scope beyond the ten paths, and it is not needed for the refusal behaviour this bundle owes.

Rely on the tracked `git diff` for archive preservation. Rejected: independent probing showed a byte change and a root-bundle rename are caught, but an untracked file, an untracked root bundle directory, an ignored file, a byte edited under `--assume-unchanged` or `--skip-worktree`, a misleading C-ID substring, and a failing `git status` subprocess all escaped. The revised instrument reads base blob bytes and compares them to filesystem bytes directly, inventories every actual archive file by exact path, and fails closed on a missing base or a failed subprocess.

Fix only the review defect and defer the selected-close defect or the teaching rows to later bundles. Rejected: the selected-close defect permits a passing close with malformed governance and skipped evidence, and the teaching rows instruct adopters incorrectly; the policy forbids carrying a known defect forward, and these repairs share one boundary and are small.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: The exact number of post-change whole-canonical lines and bytes, and therefore the literal pin values, are measured during implementation, not projected here. The spec binds the relation, not the figure; no mirror-inclusive total is used.

Whether an invalid selected record throws with distinct reason tokens or one shared invalid-selected-record reason is plan/implementation detail; the binding requirement is that the write is refused and the ledger bytes are unchanged.

The F177 / `C-ROADMAP-XML` archived-artifact reader question (`registry.xml:68`) conflicts with the later current-only policy. It is disclosed and left to that separate roadmap charter; this bundle does not authorize the reader and does not convert the record.

Current-close refusal scenario. A bundle is created, approved, and applied through the real CLI, then its selected `spec.xml` or `plan.xml` is mutated one input at a time: missing spec, malformed spec XML, wrong root tag, wrapper id not equal to the directory or `--change`, missing required section, empty criterion, explicit incomplete `CloseEvidence`, a legacy `<Criterion>` carrying an explicit `CloseEvidence`, two direct `CloseEvidence` blocks on one `AC-*`, nested `CloseEvidence`, a present non-applied status, missing plan, malformed plan, and plan id mismatch. Each mutation makes `ngrace gate verdict --outcome pass` refuse and leaves `run-ledger.xml` byte-identical, and exact restoration restores the passing result. A Command that mutates the selected plan bytes during evaluation is refused by the plan-byte snapshot guard. The failing-command control still refuses with an unchanged ledger, and a legitimate `outcome=fail` still records the failed-command evaluations. Refusal tests use otherwise-valid current-format spec/plan, fresh finding acknowledgements, and marker/ledger assertions so a missing acknowledgement cannot mask the command-result guard.

Preservation-guard scenario on a disposable copy at base. Guard A (archive): clean baseline exits 0; a tracked byte mutation, the same byte mutation under `--assume-unchanged`, the same under `--skip-worktree`, a root-bundle rename, a deletion, an extra empty root directory, an untracked file under an existing bundle, an ignored `.DS_Store`, and an untracked or ignored file whose name contains the full C-ID each exit 1 and restore to 0; the exact own arrival and an added empty nested `run/` directory stay 0; an unavailable base exits non-zero. Guard B (bounded writes): clean and all-ten-edits-plus-own-arrival exit 0; an outside-scope tracked edit, that edit under `--assume-unchanged`, that edit under `--skip-worktree`, an outside-scope tracked addition, an outside-scope tracked deletion, and a persistent tracked candidate-lock path each exit 1 and restore to 0. Both guards compare bytes and identities only; no archive content is parsed or executed, and filenames with spaces and quotes are handled losslessly.
